g.text: The TLB: a cache of translations
a few thousand entries, on the CPU
then fill the TLB and access the byte
Walking 512 MB one byte per 4 KB page: 92% of the accesses miss the TLB. The same walk with 2 MB pages: almost none.
Most programs hit almost always, because they use the same pages again and again;
the table is read rarely, and translation costs nothing you can see.
The kernel has to flush or tag the TLB when it switches address spaces: part of what a context switch costs (lecture 06).
